summary: The accepted scope is materially larger than the current inline REPL: it requires a shared execution/event contract, a real session store, and a distinct TUI lifecycle. The main blockers are the stale server proxy contract, incomplete cancellation/auth propagation, and command/rendering APIs coupled directly to AgentREPL and stdout.

suggestions.title: Define a presentation-neutral turn event protocol first
suggestions.rationale: Current AgentREPL handles strings and a final AIMessage directly, while the renderer owns terminal output. The server and daemon paths expose different shapes, so both Textual and inline mode need a common typed event stream covering text deltas, tool lifecycle, completion, failure, and cancellation.

suggestions.title: Reconcile ServerAgentProxy with the canonical server API
suggestions.rationale: The proxy calls /api/agent/{name}, /api/agents, and locally simulates streaming in fixed 50-character chunks. The server handler documents and registers /api/v1/agents/chat/{agent_id}, whose streamed response is chunked text followed by a \n\x00 metadata envelope. Server mode cannot satisfy live progress, usage, tools, or cancellation until this versioned transport is explicitly selected and parsed.

suggestions.title: Specify the authenticated identity boundary for server mode
suggestions.rationale: The CLI defaults to user_id='cli-user' and the HTTP proxy sends that body field, while AgentTalk gives an explicit request user_id priority over resolved authentication. The proxy also drops permission_context and most kwargs. Define token/device-code transport, server-side identity precedence, and PBAC tests before allowing resume or tool execution through --server.

suggestions.title: Add a session repository and an explicit resume contract
suggestions.rationale: Input history is an InMemoryHistory created inside run(), display history is a local list, and session_id is regenerated only in memory. Persistent input history and prior session resume therefore need a defined store, schema, file permissions/locking, agent-user isolation, a CLI selection or --session-id surface, and a clear distinction between display history and bot-owned conversation memory.

suggestions.title: Decouple slash commands from AgentREPL and its renderer
suggestions.rationale: Handlers directly mutate repl.config and repl.history, write through repl.renderer, and /quit raises SystemExit. The factory command additionally constructs CLIHumanChannel from the renderer console, which cannot work unchanged inside Textual. Define a command context/result interface with input, output, session, and cancellation capabilities, then adapt it for inline and TUI modes; preserve daemon command registration through that interface.

suggestions.title: Make cancellation an explicit turn lifecycle
suggestions.rationale: The current loop catches KeyboardInterrupt but does not track an active task, handle asyncio.CancelledError as a user-visible state, or explicitly close the async stream. Textual worker cancellation and HTTP disconnects must close the iterator, restore terminal state, preserve partial output as interrupted, and prevent a cancelled turn from being recorded as completed. The contract should state that remote tool rollback is not guaranteed.

suggestions.title: Define live tool-event semantics instead of inferring them from text
suggestions.rationale: BaseBot.ask_stream currently yields text and a final AIMessage; the REPL's streamed history explicitly says tool calls are not tracked, and the server emits tool_calls only in the final envelope. Daemon proxy events are reduced to formatted strings. Specify event IDs, ordering, start/progress/completion/error states, argument/result redaction and size limits, and capability fallback for backends without live events.

suggestions.title: Make display ownership and output injection explicit
suggestions.rationale: The current renderer and REPL construct separate Consoles forced to sys.__stdout__, force terminal rendering, and the streaming path writes directly to sys.stdout. A TUI must own the screen while logs, authentication prompts, command output, and model events are routed through controlled sinks. Replace implicit global stdout assumptions with an injected presentation target and test that only one owner emits terminal control sequences.

suggestions.title: Implement mode selection before choosing the input mechanism
suggestions.rationale: The Click command currently has no --ui option, always constructs the prompt REPL, and invokes an agent picker whenever the name is absent. Add a central auto|inline|tui decision using both stdin/stdout TTY state and TERM, require an agent name for non-TTY execution, and use a separate line-oriented input path for pipes so it never emits alternate-screen or picker control sequences.

suggestions.title: Build a backend-by-mode test matrix, not only mock no-raise tests
suggestions.rationale: Existing CLI tests mostly assert that mocked rendering does not raise and cover only the inline REPL. Add deterministic event-stream tests for standalone, canonical HTTP, and daemon adapters; TUI interaction tests for submit/navigation/auto-follow/completion/cancel; PTY checks for resize, SIGINT, EOF, large paste, cleanup, and terminal restoration; and pipe checks for plain output and exit status.

suggestions.title: Pin and lazily load a resolver-verified Textual version
suggestions.rationale: The core package supports Python >=3.11,<3.14 and currently declares Rich and prompt_toolkit but no Textual. Add a bounded Textual dependency only after uv resolution is verified across all supported Python versions, and import the TUI module lazily so non-agent commands and inline fallback retain their existing startup behavior. Textual's worker lifecycle should be tested against the explicit active-turn task contract.
